one_liner: Harvest has a broad, publicly documented REST API and an official, usable MCP server. The unresolved question for a new developer is whether Harvest’s free plan or trial permits creation of API credentials.

auth.notes: The docs describe OAuth2 for integrations used by other users and personal access tokens for API access.

access.notes: Harvest says its free version is available to anyone, and its API documentation says a Personal Access Token can be created in the Developers section of Harvest ID. The quotes do not restrict token creation to paid accounts.

api.notes: The public documentation describes time tracking, expenses, projects, and more.

mcp.notes: The memo says Harvest publishes connection instructions for `https://api.harvestapp.com/mcp` and does not label the MCP connection beta or preview.

verdict.rationale: Credentials are self-serve and free, and the documented API is broad enough to be useful.

evidence.quote: If you are interested in building integrations that other users can use, you will need to register an OAuth2 Application, also known as an OAuth2 Client.
The API can be accessed by creating a Personal Access Token from the Developers section of Harvest ID.
Harvest does have a free version, and it is available for anyone to use, though it does have some limitations.
The API can be accessed by creating a Personal Access Token from the Developers section of Harvest ID.
The Harvest V2 API is a REST API that allows you to interact with your Harvest account programmatically. You can track time, log expenses, create projects, and more.
The Harvest MCP is the connection that gives an MCP-compatible assistant — such as Claude — controlled access to your Harvest account, so it can carry out time tracking tasks on your behalf.
Harvest is a time-tracking and invoicing tool designed for teams and freelancers, helping them log billable hours, manage projects, and streamline payments.

problems: The Harvest ID developers page could not be read directly. The accessible pricing and API pages did not explicitly tie token creation to the free plan or trial.
name: Harvest

verification.note: OAuth2 is required for integrations other users can use, and a Personal Access Token is documented for API access; primary oauth2 matches the third-party-integration guidance. PAT is fairly classed as bearer_token.

Inferred, not explicit: a free version is available to anyone, and an account holder creates a Personal Access Token in Harvest ID. Nothing quoted ties credentials to payment, a trial, approval, or sales. The free plan's unspecified limitations are not shown to exclude the API.
The public docs call it a REST API and describe creating/tracking time, expenses, projects, and more. That does not contradict breadth broad; public_docs is shown by the readable help pages.

Harvest's own support page describes the Harvest MCP as a working connection that lets an assistant act on an account. That supports official and generally_available; the quote does not call it beta, preview, or unlaunched. The specific mcp host URL is not in the quote.
The quote is on a Composio toolkit page for Harvest (docs.composio.dev/toolkits/harvest).
